title: Finite morphisms are projective in the projective-bundle convention
statement: Let $h:T\to S$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then $h$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]: there is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module of finite type whose projective bundle contains $T$ as a closed subscheme over $S$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 29.43.2 (Tag 0B3I), morphisms-lemma-finite-projective, together with Definition 29.43.1 (Tag 01W8), clause (1) (projective means a closed immersion into a projective bundle).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal E=h_*\mathcal O_T$, including its natural commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebra structure. The finite-morphism definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] gives that $\mathcal E$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, that $h$ is affine, and that over every affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ the inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}A$, where $A=\mathcal E(V)$ is a finite $R$-algebra. We construct a closed immersion into $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$, as required by [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0B3I (lemma-finite-projective), canonical embedding into P(h_*O_T); explicit graded-quotient verification by the worker

proof.text: Form a graded sheaf algebra $\mathcal B$ with $\mathcal B_0=\mathcal O_S$ and $\mathcal B_n=\mathcal E$ for each $n\ge1$. Write $a[n]$ for $a$ in its degree-$n$ copy. For positive $m,n$, define $a[m]b[n]=(ab)[m+n]$; let degree zero act through the given $\mathcal O_S$-algebra structure and take the unit in degree zero. Associativity, commutativity, unitality and restriction compatibility follow directly from those of $\mathcal E$, giving precisely [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. Its underlying sheaf is the categorical sum $\mathcal O_S\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ge1}\mathcal E$, hence is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-coproduct-closure]. For an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the tilde/global-sections equivalence and preservation of coproducts in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identify $\mathcal B(V)$ with $C=R\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ge1}A[n]$, with the displayed multiplication. Denote the global degree-one section $1_{\mathcal E}[1]$ by $t$.

source.place: Tag 0B3I (lemma-finite-projective), canonical embedding into P(h_*O_T); explicit graded-quotient verification by the worker

proof.text: The inclusion $\mathcal E\to\mathcal B_1$ induces a sheaf-algebra map $q:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)\to\mathcal B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra]. It is degree preserving for the symmetric-degree grading [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]: a product of $n$ degree-one generators goes to their product in $\mathcal B_n$. It is surjective in every degree. Degree zero is the identity on $\mathcal O_S$; for $n\ge1$ each local $a[n]$ is the image of $j(a)j(1)^{n-1}$. By Step 2, $\mathcal B$ and $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)$ are graded $\mathcal O_S$-algebras whose underlying modules are quasi-coherent, i.e. quasi-coherent algebras [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra], so both relative Proj schemes [def-nagata-relative-proj] are defined. Thus the surjective graded-map clause of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] supplies a closed immersion $\iota:\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal B)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E))=\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$ over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0B3I (lemma-finite-projective), canonical embedding into P(h_*O_T); explicit graded-quotient verification by the worker

proof.text: On an affine $V$ use $C=R\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ge1}A[n]$ from Step 2 and $t=1_A[1]$. Every positive-degree homogeneous element satisfies $a[n]^2=t\,(a^2)[2n-1]$. If a homogeneous prime contains $t$, primality therefore forces it to contain every positive-degree homogeneous element and hence $C_+$. Such a prime is excluded from $\operatorname{Proj}(C)$ by [def-pc-proj]. Consequently the entire Proj is the single standard open $D_+(t)$. By [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open] it is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(C_{(t),0})$. This calculation uses no integrality, reducedness, or cancellation.

source.place: Tag 0B3I (lemma-finite-projective), canonical embedding into P(h_*O_T); explicit graded-quotient verification by the worker

proof.text: Compute $C_{(t),0}$ with the fraction convention of [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. Every fraction can be represented as $a[m]/t^m$ with $m\ge1$: for a degree-zero numerator $r\in R$, multiply numerator and denominator by $t$ to obtain $\eta(r)[1]/t$. The map $a[m]/t^m\mapsto a$ is well defined, since multiplication by $t$ on every positive-degree copy of $A$ is the identity on its coefficient, so the localization equality of two such fractions is exactly equality of their coefficients. Its inverse is $a\mapsto a[1]/t$. The product and sum formulas show these are inverse $R$-algebra maps, and the degree-zero structure map becomes $\eta:R\to A$. Thus the chart of Step 4 is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}A=h^{-1}(V)$ over $V$, using spectrum functoriality [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The argument also applies when $A=0$: both localizations and both spectra are then zero or empty as appropriate.

source.place: Tag 0B3I (lemma-finite-projective), canonical embedding into P(h_*O_T); explicit graded-quotient verification by the worker

proof.text: Relative Proj restricts to the affine Proj of its section algebra, compatibly with further restriction and structure maps, by [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality]. The local isomorphisms of Steps 4--5 commute with restriction: on every affine refinement of an overlap, the same formula sends $a[m]/t^m$ to the restricted section $a$, and $t$ restricts to the degree-one unit. The inverse formulas commute as well. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to both families. Their two composites are identities on the affine-base open covers, hence are identities by uniqueness in that node. This gives an $S$-isomorphism $T\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal B)$. Composing it with the closed immersion of Step 3 is a closed immersion (the homeomorphism onto a closed set and sheaf-surjection conditions of [def-weil-closed-immersion] are preserved under precomposition with an isomorphism). Since $\mathcal E$ is finite type quasi-coherent by Step 1, [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] now says exactly that $h$ is projective in the required convention.

The item statement matches Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 0B3I (morphisms-lemma-finite-projective) read with Definition 01W8(1), with no hypothesis added and the statement unchanged. The steps check: E=h_*O_T is quasi-coherent of finite type (def-weil-finite-integral-morphism). B has B_0=O_S and B_n=E, and its sections over an affine are C=R plus positive copies of A, by the tilde/Gamma clauses (2)-(4). Sym(E)->B is graded and surjective because a[n]=q(j(a)j(1)^{n-1}), so functoriality clause (3) gives the closed immersion. In Step 4, a[n]^2=t(a^2)[2n-1] puts every prime containing t over C_+, so Proj C=D_+(t); the cover clause alone would not do this, since t does not generate C_+. In Step 5, C_(t),0 is A: equality of fractions a[m]/t^m comes down to equality of coefficients. Step 6 glues on affine refinements and never assumes an overlap is affine. I tested S empty, A=0, A=R, A=R/I, k[eps] over k, RxR, and R->A not injective; all work. Duplicate search (rg for 0B3I, lemma-finite-projective and finite/projective wording) found no node stating this; the hits are citers or unrelated statements. There are no new nodes. I accept the seven declared tool_uses as generic black boxes: none replaces a step of the sk-i-curve-zero route. The source typo the report notes (R[x]->Sym(A) where A is meant) is real and does not affect the delivery.
